{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement (MSA)

**To:** Deal Team
**From:** In-house Counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive Summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. The draft is materially unbalanced against us in four areas that we regard as deal-critical, and it contains internal contradictions that Vendor will need to resolve regardless of position.

The most serious issue is that **the Agreement has no indemnification provision at all** — the numbering jumps from Section 19 (Warranties) to Section 21 (Limitation of Liability), yet at least four surviving clauses assume indemnities exist (including § 9.3, which conditions our termination right on "the remedies required by Section 20.5," a section that does not exist). We have no Vendor IP infringement or misconduct indemnity, which is our walk-away outcome. We have inserted a new Section 20 that both supplies the indemnity and repairs the dangling cross-reference.

Second, **§ 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of Deliverables we commission and pay for**, leaving us only a revocable, non-transferable licence for the Order Form term. That is contrary to our position that we own what we pay for, and it conflicts with the perpetual, irrevocable paid-up grant Vendor has already accepted in § 13.2.

Third, a cluster of **lock-in provisions** operates together to remove any commercial exit: the § 2.1 USD 2,000,000/year three-year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights," the § 7.2 disclose-and-match gate on engaging other providers (a reverse MFN and de facto sole-supplier restriction), the second § 12.4 24-month worldwide non-compete, and the absence of any termination-for-convenience right in Section 9. Each of these independently sits at or beyond our walk-away line, and each contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor expressly acknowledges we have made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, non-compete, no-hire or minimum-volume commitment.

Fourth, we have no exit path for our data: Section 10 addresses access cut-off and refunds only, with no data return, export or deletion obligation anywhere in the Agreement.

More positively, several provisions already meet our preferred position in full and require **no redline**: limitation of liability (Section 21 — mutual cap at the greater of trailing 12-month Fees and USD 1,000,000, with a full uncapped Excluded Claims list), assignment and change of control (Section 24), audit rights against us (Section 22), auto-renewal mechanics (§§ 8.2–8.3, including a Vendor reminder obligation with deadline extension), the performance warranty package (Section 19), and Vendor's insurance covenant (Section 18). Governing law (§ 28.1, Singapore) is a discrete fix that Vendor should accept readily, since § 28.2 already confers exclusive jurisdiction on the New York County courts.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary / Position |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Critical** | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 9.3 (dangling reference to § 20.5) | No indemnity anywhere; numbering skips from 19 to 21 while §§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 all presuppose one. Inserted new Section 20 (Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity, narrow Customer indemnity, procedure, IP exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies at 20.5). |
| 2 | **Critical** | IP — Ownership of Deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 14.2 | Vendor owns all Deliverables; we get a revocable, term-limited licence. Reversed ownership to Customer with Vendor assignment; Vendor Technology untouched under §§ 14.3 / 13.2. |
| 3 | **Critical** | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Compliant** | § 21.1 | Mutual cap at greater of trailing 12-month Fees and USD 1,000,000; mutual consequential-damages exclusion with restoration/notification costs confirmed as direct; full uncapped Excluded Claims list. No redline. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Compliant** | § 24.1 | Consent-free assignment to Affiliates/M&A successors; Vendor restricted; § 24.4 bars Vendor repricing or exit on our change of control. No redline. |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 2.1 (with § 7.2) | Take-or-pay lock-in plus match-or-disclose gate = de facto sole-supplier restriction; contradicts § 12.3. Delete § 7.2; make § 2.1 non-exclusive with any minimum Order Form-specific and reducible on Vendor failure. |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 2.1 | Take-or-pay operates as a Customer-payable penalty for remaining contract value; contradicts §§ 7.1 and 12.3. Delete; confirm any early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees as the sole liquidated amount. |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 14.2 | Deliverable licence is revocable, non-transferable and term-limited, conflicting with the perpetual irrevocable grant in § 13.2. Make it perpetual, irrevocable, paid-up, extended to Affiliates/contractors, transferable under § 13.3, with §§ 13.2–13.3 controlling. |
| 8 | High | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Open-ended reverse MFN requiring us to disclose and match third-party offers, with no scope, time limit or carve-outs; contradicts § 12.3. Delete — no Vendor-granted MFN elsewhere, so nothing beneficial is lost. |
| 9 | High | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 | Three-year USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay with express denial of reduction or termination rights; undercuts §§ 9.1–9.3 and 10.2. Delete; pay only for Services ordered or used. Fallback offered in comment. |
| 10 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 (second) | 24 months post-term, any territory, undefined scope, sweeping in acquisitions and internal development; contradicts § 12.3. Delete, with narrowed fallback offered. |
| 11 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § 9 (Termination) | Only for-cause, insolvency and security/SLA/law/IP triggers; no no-fault exit across a three-year term (§ 8.1) reinforced by § 2.1. Added 30-day convenience right with pro-rata refund, no penalty, no reciprocal Vendor right, and conformed § 2.1. |
| 12 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Compliant** | § 22.1 | Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site where practicable, independent auditor under confidentiality; Vendor bears cost absent >5% underpayment; no system access. No redline. |
| 13 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 28.1 | Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction is outside our accepted list and contradicts § 28.2 (New York County). Replaced governing law and forum with New York, aligning § 28.1 with § 28.2. |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 | One-way 24-month no-hire covering all Vendor employees "regardless of how the employee applies," with no advertising or unsolicited-applicant carve-out; contradicts § 12.3. Delete; mutual 12-month fallback offered. |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | **Compliant** | § 8.2 | Successive 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder with deadline extension if missed; § 8.3 caps uplift at lesser of CPI and 3%. No redline. |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 10.1 | No data return, export, transition or deletion obligation anywhere; § 16.5 defers to a non-existent Section 11. Inserted § 10.3: up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, data return in machine-readable format within 30 days, certified deletion thereafter. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Compliant** (repaired) | § 19.1 | Failed period check was a phrasing false negative — § 19.2's "ninety days" meets the 90-day floor and runs from the later of delivery or acceptance; hosted Services conform throughout the subscription term. Remedy ladder in § 19.4 is non-exclusive. No redline; optional clerical conforming of the numeral at signature. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Compliant** | § 18.1 | CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber and privacy USD 5M, workers' comp and employer's liability USD 1M, through term plus one year; § 18.2 confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities. No redline. |

---

## 3. Walk-Away Items

The following findings are identified in our verified analysis as being at or beyond the playbook walk-away line. We should not sign without movement on each.

1. **No Vendor indemnity (§ 20 absent).** The complete absence of an IP infringement and misconduct indemnity is expressly the playbook walk-away outcome. Vendor cannot credibly resist here — its own drafting in §§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 assumes the indemnity exists, and § 9.3 is unworkable without § 20.5.
2. **Take-or-pay lock-in (§ 2.1).** A three-year USD 2,000,000/year commitment "without reduction or termination rights" is the walk-away scenario under MINCOMMIT and is below the walk-away line under EXCLUSIVITY. It is also prohibited as a Customer-payable penalty under LD. Fallback if commercially essential: a 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, with true-up rather than penalty.
3. **No termination for convenience (§ 9).** Combined with the three-year term in § 8.1 and the § 2.1 language, we have no no-fault exit — the playbook walk-away scenario. Our redline adds a 30-day right with pro-rata refund.
4. **Reverse MFN (§ 7.2).** An unlimited obligation to disclose and match better third-party terms, with no scope, time limit or comparison carve-outs, is effectively the walk-away position. Deletion is the preferred remedy and costs us nothing.
5. **Deliverable ownership and licence (§ 14.2).** Vendor ownership of paid-for work product is contrary to our position, and the revocable, at-will, term-limited licence sits at the walk-away end of the LICENSE rule.
6. **One-way 24-month no-hire (§ 12.4).** Covering all Vendor employees regardless of how they apply, with no carve-outs, this sits at the walk-away line.
7. **Exclusive foreign venue (§ 28.1).** Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction approaches the walk-away position; the internal conflict with § 28.2 should make this a straightforward correction.

---

## 4. Next Steps

1. **Issue the redline** as marked, prioritising the four critical/structural items: new Section 20 (indemnification), § 14.2 (Deliverable ownership and licence), the § 2.1 / § 7.2 / § 12.4 lock-in cluster, and the new termination-for-convenience right in Section 9.
2. **Lead with the internal inconsistencies** in our cover note. Section 12.3 already records Vendor's acknowledgement that we have made no exclusivity, MFN, non-compete, no-hire or minimum-volume commitment, which directly contradicts §§ 2.1, 7.2 and both instances of § 12.4. Similarly, § 28.2 contradicts § 28.1, and § 9.3 cross-refers to a § 20.5 that does not exist. These are conforming corrections as much as negotiating positions.
3. **Flag the drafting gaps to Vendor's counsel** for confirmation that we are working from a complete document: the missing Section 20, the missing Section 11 (to which § 16.5 defers for Customer Data), the empty Section 23 heading (Records and Customer Assurance), and the duplicate § 12.4 numbering.
4. **Confirm the commercial mandate** on § 2.1 with the business owner before we tender the fallback. If a minimum is genuinely required, we will offer the 12-month, reducible, true-up structure and hold the line that any early-termination fee is capped at three months' Fees as the sole liquidated amount.
5. **Do not reopen the compliant provisions.** Sections 18, 19, 21, 22, 24 and §§ 8.2–8.3 already meet or exceed our preferred position; we should protect them and avoid inviting Vendor to trade them against the items above. The only optional change is a clerical conforming of "ninety days" to "ninety (90) days" in § 19.2 at signature.
6. **Sequence the close.** Once the redline is returned, we will re-verify that the new § 20.5 resolves the § 9.3 cross-reference, that the amended § 2.1 does not negate the new convenience right, and that the § 14.2 precedence language leaves §§ 13.2–13.3 controlling.

*This memo reflects only the verified findings supplied for this review and the sections cited within them.*"}
